Cannaceae.key_door: one fertile petaloid stamen + flat petaloid style + multiovulate inferior ovary + warty many-seeded capsule

Marantaceae.key_door: pulvinus + one fertile stamen + hooded/callose staminodes + hook-style trigger + one ovule per locule

lineage_lesson: Both families are rhizomatous broad-leaved Zingiberales with highly asymmetric flowers and only one fertile stamen. Split them by the pollination machinery and ovule/seed plan: Cannaceae is multiovulate and many-seeded; Marantaceae uses specialized trigger staminodes and usually one ovule per locule.
species_notes: Canna glauca is accepted and native in Texas under current Kew; strict target-zone county approval remains a separate species workflow.

Thalia geniculata is accepted; Kew treats the species as native from the southeastern U.S. into tropical America, while FNA emphasizes Florida/Louisiana U.S. records. Texas/project-range resolution remains species-level.
guardrails: Family/genus recognition only; no species promotion.
Do not identify either family from broad canna-like leaves alone.
Use flower mechanics and ovule/fruit structure as the primary family split.
